nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
سَأَلَ سائِلٌ: this is the reading of the people of Kufa and the people of Basra, pronouncing both with hamza. Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿraj and Nāfiʿ read سَأَلَ سائِلٌ [i.e. "sāla sāʾilun"] [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described]:
the first without hamza and the second with hamza. This reading has two aspects. One of them is that «سال» is from "al-sayl" (flowing), i.e. it poured down. The other is that "sāla" is said in the sense of "saʾala", not that it is derived from it [by lightening], because this is not the lightening of the hamza; if it were from it, it could only be by substitution for the hamza, and that is far-fetched and anomalous (shādhdh). Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān hold that it is from the hamzated [root], and that an error was made about it in transmitting from Nāfiʿ, and that he only used to pronounce the hamza between-between (bayna bayna). Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a far-fetched interpretation and an accusation of error against everyone who transmitted from Nāfiʿ. The right view about it is that Sībawayh reported "siltu asālu" in the sense of "saʾaltu" (I asked); so the origin of "sāla" is "sawala", and when the wāw was vowelled and what preceded it was vowelled, it was turned into an alif — and like it is "khiftu". "Sāʾil" is hamzated in its original form if it is from "saʾala"; if it is from "sāla", the origin is "sāwil", on the pattern fāʿil: the wāw was turned into an alif with a quiescent alif before it, and two quiescent letters do not meet, so a hamza was substituted for the alif, as in "ṣāʾim" and "khāʾif". بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
لِلْكافِرينَ: the view of al-Farrāʾ ]
is that the implied form is "of a punishment for the disbelievers", and in his view "li-l-kāfirīna" cannot be attached to "wāqiʿ". Abū Jaʿfar said: the apparent sense of the Qur'an is otherwise than what he said, and the exegetes are against his view. Mujāhid said: and falling in the Hereafter. Al-Ḥasan said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
سَأَلَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ, and they said: for whom is it, upon whom will it fall? So Allah the Exalted revealed: لِلْكافِرينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دافِعٌ.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: It has been said: "al-maʿārij" are the steps of Paradise. Ibn [Abī] Najīḥ reported from Mujāhid, who said: the sky.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «يعرج» [masculine],
treating the plural as masculine. فِي يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned several views about it. The highest of what has been said about it is from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: it is the Day of Resurrection; and the meaning is that the measure of Allah's — Mighty and Majestic — reckoning with creation on it, His rewarding them and punishing them, is the measure of fifty thousand years were anyone other than Him the reckoner. This is indicated by the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how long this day is!" He said: "For the believer it is lighter than an obligatory prayer that he performs."

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: فَاصْبِرْ: in the face of their harm. صَبْراً جَمِيلًا: with no anxious complaint in it.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: Because they do not believe in it. It has been said: the pronoun in "innahum" is for the disbelievers and the one in "yarawnahu" is for the punishment.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: Because it is bound to be, and everything bound to be is near.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: The implied form may be: "this will happen", or "they will see them, on the day the sky is like molten brass". "Yawm" was put in construct with the verb because it is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), and was conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: The plural of "ʿihna"; one also says "ʿuhūn".

nahhas-irab:10-11.t:
يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ: there is disagreement among the scholars about this pronoun. From Ibn ʿAbbās: the close friend is shown his close friend, i.e. he sees him and recognizes him, then flees from him. This is one view. Ibn Abī Najīḥ reported from Mujāhid: the believers are shown the disbelievers. And from Ibn Zayd: in the Fire, the followers are shown those they followed. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The most correct of these views is the first, because the close friend has already been mentioned, so for the pronoun to refer back to him is more fitting than for it to refer back to something not mentioned. يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ:
«يومئذ» was made indeclinable »
because it was put in construct with something not inflected; if you wish, you put it in the genitive by the construct, and read مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ [i.e. "yawmiʾidhin"].

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: That is, then the ransoming would save him, because يَفْتَدِي indicates ransoming.

nahhas-irab:15-16.t:
كَلَّا: a good stopping point. إِنَّها لَظى نَزَّاعَةً لِلشَّوى: there is disagreement among the grammarians about this. "Laẓā" may be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from your saying «ها», with "nazzāʿa" the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». It has been said: لَظى is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «إن», and نَزَّاعَةً is a second khabar, or a badal, or [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). And it has been said: «ها» is an allusion (kināya) to the story [i.e. the pronoun of the matter], and لَظى نَزَّاعَةً are a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and together they are the khabar of «إنّ». Abū ʿUbayd permitted نَزَّاعَةً
in the accusative, and reported that it was not read so. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd does not permit the accusative here, because it cannot be anything but "stripping off the scalp", and that is not how a ḥāl (circumstantial) behaves.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: Figurative (majāz), because it is reported that its keepers call out: "Bring us whoever turned away and turned his back on obeying Allah." Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: it calls whoever turned away from obeying Allah and turned his back on His Book and His right.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: That is, he put the wealth in a container and did not pay the dues from it. One says "waʿaytu al-ʿilma" (I retained the knowledge) and "awʿaytu al-matāʿa" (I put the goods in a container).

nahhas-irab:19-21.t: إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً (19) إِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً (20) وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً (21): خُلِقَ is in the position of the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and you put هَلُوعاً in the accusative as an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial) (ḥāl muqaddara). "Al-halūʿ", according to what the lexicographers report, is one who, in a state of poverty, shows what he should not show of anxious complaint and lack of fortitude, and in wealth shows what he should not show of withholding the obligatory due and lack of gratitude. He has explained this by His saying: إِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً. You put جَزُوعاً and مَنُوعاً in the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of "halūʿ"; the implied form may also be "he became such".

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: Conjoined to it. Saʿīd reported that Qatāda said: the obligatory charity (zakat). Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَالَّذِينَ فِي أَمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَعْلُومٌ: he said: He means apart from the charity, by which he maintains ties of kinship, strengthens a weak person, bears the burden of a dependant, or helps a deprived person.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: it is soundly reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "al-maḥrūm" is the one denied the means of livelihood. From Qatāda: "al-sāʾil" is the one who begs with his palm, and "al-maḥrūm" is the one who refrains, i.e. who does not beg; and each has a right over you, O son of Adam. From Ibn Zayd: «المحروم» is the one whose crops have burned.

nahhas-irab:26-34.t:
فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وَراءَ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ (31) وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَماناتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ (32) وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهاداتِهِمْ قائِمُونَ (33) وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ (34)
وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ عَذابِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ: in the position of the accusative; all of it is conjoined to the naʿt (adjective) of "al-muṣallīn", and likewise وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ, and likewise وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهاداتِهِمْ قائِمُونَ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Ḥasan is بِشَهاداتِهِمْ [Translator's note: the vowelled text shows the plural; the variant ascribed to them is evidently the singular "bi-shahādatihim", as the following explanation shows].
Abū Jaʿfar said: "shahāda" is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so for that reason a group read it in the singular; it may also be a singular indicating a plural. Likewise وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: Accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ عِزِينَ: the plural of "ʿiza", pluralized with wāw and nūn although it contains the sign of the feminine, [the plural] being compensation for what was dropped from it. There is another dialect form: one says "marartu bi-qawmin ʿizīnin", placing the inflection on the nūn.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
The reading of al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa is أَنْ يُدْخَلَ [i.e. "an yadkhula"]
with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the khāʾ. [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described.] Abū Jaʿfar said:
The verse is difficult. Among what has been said about it is that the meaning is: what is the matter with those who disbelieve, hastening towards you with denial of you? And it has been said: [hastening] to listen to you so as to find fault with you. عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ عِزِينَ: that is, divided in their religions while opposing Islam — does every man of them hope to be rewarded for this and enter Paradise? And it has been said:
does every man of them hope to be saved from the punishment despite this deed? — because the meaning of "entering Paradise" is being saved from the punishment.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: كَلَّا: a rebuttal of them. إِنَّا خَلَقْناهُمْ مِمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ: He reminded them of their lowliness, and that they were created only from a drop of fluid; so how would they deserve reward if they have not done righteous deeds? As Qatāda said: you were created from filth, O son of Adam, so fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشارِقِ وَالْمَغارِبِ: Abū Ẓabyān said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: the sun has every day a place of rising and a place of setting that it did not have the day before; and that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشارِقِ وَالْمَغارِبِ. "Lā" is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis; we know of no disagreement about that. They only disagreed about «لا أقسم» [in Sūrat al-Qiyāma] because it is the beginning of the sūra, and they disliked saying "redundant at the beginning of the sūra"; the grammarians agree that «لا» and «ما» are not added redundantly at the beginning of speech, so the discussion there was more difficult. The answer to the oath is: إِنَّا لَقادِرُونَ.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: That is, they cannot frustrate Us or escape Us, because whoever has a thing escape him and does not catch up with it has been outstripped by it.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا وَيَلْعَبُوا: an answer (jawāb), carrying the sense of a condition; whereas in another place ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ [al-Anʿām: 91], because that is not an answer. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd claimed that the difference between them is that when it is with the nūn, they are in that state [at the time], and when it is without the nūn, it is for the future. يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ: a badal (substitute) from it. مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ سِراعاً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ: the reading of al-Ḥasan is إِلى نُصُبٍ [i.e. "naṣbin"] [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described],
and likewise it is reported from Zayd ibn Thābit and Abū al-ʿĀliya: that is, racing towards goals. Al-Ḥasan said: they used to gather in the early morning and sit, and when the sun rose they would rush to their idols (anṣāb). Al-Aʿraj said: "ilā naṣbin" means to a banner. Abū Jaʿfar said: its implied form in Arabic is "to a banner that has been set up (nuṣiba naṣban)".

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
خاشِعَةً أَبْصارُهُمْ: that is, humbled and submissive because of what has befallen them. "Khāshiʿatan" is accusative by "tarhaquhum" or by "yakhrujūna". تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ: that is, covers them. ذلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ:
It has been said: [the day] which the polytheists of Quraysh were promised, and they did not believe it. [Translator's note: the text reads «الذي كانوا مشركو قريش يوعدون به», with a grammatical irregularity in «كانوا مشركو».]
